title: How a shared state is described determines whether AI agents synchronize: data and code
description:
Research data and code accompanying the study by Takahiro Ezaki, Naoto Imura and Katsuhiro Nishinari, How a shared state is described determines whether AI agents synchronize.

Version 1.1.0 retains the original 15 acquisition groups and adds the September 2026 Claude controlled-field concentration sweep: 25,920 accepted responses in two blocks, the separate preflight journal, immutable attempt records, stimuli, protocols, and frozen analysis tables. It includes the response-count audit for 507,112 valid responses in the reported analyses, the persistence check, and the current figure-generation scripts and 44 PDF display assets.

Offline analysis and figure reproduction use recorded data and require no provider API calls. The README distinguishes current figures from the historical v1.0.0 figure pipeline and gives verification commands. Exact re-acquisition depends on provider model availability.
